newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Seven in A$1.2 mln payout with presenter.
newsitem.headline: Seven in A$1.2 mln payout with presenter.

text.p: Current affairs television presenter Jana Wendt on Thursday ended her dispute with Seven Network Ltd and agreed to resign following a $1.2 million out-of-court settlement.

Speaking to reporters outside the New South Wales Industrial Commission, Seven lawyer Stephen Rothman said Wendt had accepted the network's offer after more than 12 hours of "acrimonious" private negotiations.
"Jana Wendt has accepted an offer made by Channel Seven the week before the case commenced of $1.2 million...we'll each be paying our own costs," Rothman said.

"Channel Seven is very satisfied and comfortable with the settlement...and looks forward to putting the matter behind it." Wendt, one of Australia's best known journalists and presenter of Seven's current affairs flagship show Witness, was stood down in January after she complained about the editorial direction of the programme.
She claimed Witness had become trivial, despite promises made to her from Seven that it would deal only with high-quality, hard-hitting issues.

Wendt said her reputation as a serious journalist, garnered on the rival Nine Network, had been seriously damaged and she had sought to have her contract with Seven terminated in addition to damages of $6 million.
